newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japanese banks reject fund request from PM's party.
newsitem.headline: Japanese banks reject fund request from PM's party.

text.p: Japanese banks have turned down requests from the country's largest party for political funds, a senior official of the Federation of Bankers' Associations of Japan told a news conference on Thursday.

The official said the federation received letters requesting 700 million yen ($6.4 million) in political funds on July 8 from the Liberal Democratic Party (LDP), the main party in the ruling coalition.

"I thought this request was odd, in light of the LDP's policy hammered out earlier this year to refrain from receiving political funds from banks associated with failed housing loan firms," the federation official said.
The official said he had visited the LDP headquarters to discuss the issue with a senior official handling finances.
The LDP accepted the federation's view that the request seemed to go against the party's policy and withdrew the request, the federation official said.
"We confirmed with the LDP that the party's policy was to refrain from receiving political funds from banks. We turned down the request for political funds in accordance with that policy," he said.

Finance Minister Wataru Kubo told reporters on Wednesday that he believed the coalition parties should honour an earlier pledge to refrain from receiving any political contributions from the industry.
Kubo is a member of the Social Democratic Party.
Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto, who is the president of the LDP, was meeting his coalition partners on Thursday to discuss the date for a general election.
